clue.text: Estimates increase no end — shocks all round

indicators.note: all round says the shocks word encircles the other piece

parts.note: to shock is to appal, so shocks gives APPALS

indicators.note: no end tells us to drop the final letter of the word for increase

parts.note: to increase something is to raise it

explanation.surface: Forecasts keep climbing, with nasty surprises on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: Appraisals are valuations or assessments, the plural noun matching the estimates of a surveyor or valuer.

clue.text: Suit of a particular colour reduced in length

indicators.note: reduced in length means shortened, so the colour word loses its final letter

parts.note: green is one particular colour

explanation.surface: A matching outfit in one shade that has been shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit someone is to be acceptable to them, so if a plan suits it fits, as when foods agree with you.

clue.text: Artist featured in cheap jewelry catalogue

parts.note: paste is glass used to make imitation gems
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A painter whose work appears in a bargain jewellery brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastelist is an artist who works in pastels, coloured chalky crayons.

clue.text: In disarray, like porcelain after bovine escapade?

definitions.meaning: after a bull in a china shop the crockery would be strewn round the whole store

explanation.surface: Breakables wrecked after a bull gets loose in a china shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered or disorganised; literally it describes broken china spread across a whole store.

clue.text: Impose capital punishment, or less extreme sentence

definitions.meaning: to hang someone, slang being to ... their neck
a term in prison, slang for a stint inside

explanation.surface: A judge weighing execution against a milder jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch is slang both for hanging someone and for a spell of imprisonment.

clue.text: Clean combination of various continental articles

parts.note: la is the French or Spanish feminine definite article
un is the French masculine indefinite article
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A recipe for a cleaning agent made of assorted European items.
explanation.walkthrough: Three articles from European languages: LA (French 'the'), UN (French 'a') and DER (German 'the'); 'various' says they come from different languages.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash and iron clothes, so to clean them.

clue.text: Apparently good investment in City, of heroic proportions

indicators.note: investment in, read as putting something into, places the good word within the City letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: A sound-looking financial stake in the Square Mile turns out to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital is the City of London, abbreviated EC; 'Apparently' is just colour suggesting the investment only looks good.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic poem, so as an adjective it means grand, vast and heroic in scale.

clue.text: Fussily dress in skirt with very soft edging

indicators.note: edging says the very soft letters form a border round the skirt word

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft
to skirt something is to run round its edge, its rim

explanation.surface: Dressing elaborately in a skirt trimmed with delicate fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' looks like the garment, but it is the edge, a RIM; PP is the musical marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom or dress oneself with fussy care.

clue.text: Person who reduces text, making study more concentrated

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
something more concentrated is denser

explanation.surface: An editor who boils copy down, making a piece of research tighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who condenses a text abridges or shortens it.

clue.text: One racked with guilt merely produces an affirmation of agreement

definitions.text: One racked with guilt merely produces
definitions.meaning: a person tormented by guilt does no more than confess, pouring out the facts to the listener
a colloquial reply meaning I know that only too well

explanation.surface: A guilty conscience only yields a nod of assent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: a guilt-wracked person is spilling a confession to you.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is an emphatic way of saying you entirely agree, having experienced the same thing.

clue.text: Neat getaways suit this thief

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a thief who likes cattle making off is a stock thief, not a tidy escaper

explanation.surface: A burglar who prefers a clean, tidy escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but it is the old word for cattle or oxen, so the getaways are of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle, horses or sheep, the cattle being the neat of the clue.

clue.text: Ideal university head, a Scot?

parts.note: the head of something is its top
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, so it stands for a Scot

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the perfect vice-chancellor would be Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes a perfect imagined society, so it means idealised or impossibly perfect.

clue.text: Never troubled by a delinquent or dispirited

indicators.note: troubled suggests stirring up, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth seen as a delinquent

explanation.surface: Someone untroubled by a young offender, or else fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' shuffles NEVER and A into ENERVA; TED is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth-cult figure associated with delinquency.
explanation.definitionFit: Enervated means drained of energy or vigour, close to weakened and lacking spirit.

clue.text: It's not round Europe this currency's circulated

indicators.note: circulated means moved about, so the letters of the continent are mixed once the round letter goes

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that this money is not legal tender across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not round' tells you to remove O from EUROPE, and 'circulated' rearranges the remaining EURPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the monetary unit of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Keen to do this civic official's job?

definitions.text: Keen to do this civic official's job?

parts.words: Keen to do this civic official's job?
parts.note: keen here is not eager but to wail or cry out, which is what a town announcer does for a living

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastic about a council post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but as a verb it means to wail loudly, and a town officer's job was to cry out announcements.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who shouted public announcements in the streets.

clue.text: Cheese offered by someone in club pet devours

indicators.note: devours means swallows up, so the pet word wraps round the club person

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
a member is someone who belongs to a club

explanation.surface: A cheese supplied by a club regular whose cat is gobbling it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft creamy French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Book with stiff paper

parts.note: something stiff is hard
The Times is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A volume bound in thick card.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard Times is a Charles Dickens novel; the paper is The Times, the very newspaper printing the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is an 1854 novel by Charles Dickens, so it is a book by title.

clue.text: Unhappy race discovers rising in the interior

indicators.note: in the interior puts the reversed piece inside the race word

parts.note: a mile is a classic running race

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the word upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to discover something is to uncover or bare it

explanation.surface: A dejected people learn of an uprising inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovers' reads as finds, but it means uncovers; 'rising' signals an upward reading in a down clue, and 'race' looks like a people but is a running event.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable means wretchedly unhappy or downcast.

clue.text: Unequalled as stick-rubbing scouts?

definitions.meaning: scouts rubbing sticks together to light a fire are presumably short of anything to strike

explanation.surface: Boy scouts showing off their supreme skill at fire-lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means having no equal; read literally, it means having no matches to light a fire.

clue.text: Retired model who revealed a lot?

parts.note: ex means former, as of someone retired
a model is someone who poses, a poser

explanation.surface: A former fashion model who once bared a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'model who revealed a lot', the question mark flagging a playful idea of someone who exposed things.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposer is one who uncovers or reveals things to view.

clue.text: Place fully content to admit one union

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the satisfied word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy fully
the Roman numeral for one is I
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: Somewhere entirely satisfied to let in a single trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to put it in a particular position or location.

clue.text: Electronic device in wheel, a servo-mechanism

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is contained within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An engineering note about a gadget fitted to a wheel's control system.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is an optical device producing an intense narrow beam of light, an electronic instrument.

clue.text: Old king making millions, one finally turned glum

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million or millions
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: turned says the word for glum is read backwards

parts.note: glum means sad

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler who made a fortune but ended up miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SAD to DAS; 'finally' only says this piece comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas was the legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Exclamation of annoyance after which one must take advantage

definitions.meaning: an old expletive, as in what the devil

definitions.text: after which one must take advantage
definitions.meaning: in tennis, from forty-all a player must win the advantage point before the game

explanation.surface: A curse muttered by someone told they must seize the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advantage' is the tennis score that follows forty-all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a mild oath meaning the devil, and also the tennis score of forty-all.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical leader courts publicity outside church

indicators.note: outside says the publicity letters sit round the courts word

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, that is, publicity
atria are open courts inside buildings, the plural of atrium

explanation.surface: A senior cleric seeking press attention beyond his church's walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is a bishop of the highest rank in the Orthodox and some other churches.

clue.text: Male facility for showing courage

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an art is a skill or facility

explanation.surface: A man's knack for being brave.
explanation.definitionFit: To have heart is to have courage or spirit.

clue.text: Bird and insect endlessly trying to get even

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the insect word is cut off

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: An ostrich-like bird and a bug both trying to settle a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulous means eager to emulate or rival someone, striving to match or outdo them.

clue.text: A learner, say, about to get support with some maths

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the say abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, means the same as say
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A novice reckons on extra help with a mathematics lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics using symbols for numbers, so it is one part of maths.

clue.text: Box, perhaps, that's made of wood

definitions.meaning: box is an evergreen shrub or small hardwood plant, an example of the kind
a trunk and branches are wooden, so the thing is literally formed of timber

explanation.surface: A remark that a crate is built from timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is the box shrub, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a species of the woody plant family, and any such plant consists of wood.

clue.text: One bishop meeting temptress with payment is unholy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
Eve tempted Adam with the apple in Genesis
rent is a regular payment for a home

explanation.surface: A cleric meeting a seductress for money is behaving sinfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means showing a lack of respect for sacred things, hence disrespectful or impious.
